newsitem.title: USA: CompuServe posts Q4 oper loss $12.2 mln.
newsitem.headline: CompuServe posts Q4 oper loss $12.2 mln.

text.p: CompuServe Corp reported a $12.2 million loss for the fourth quarter ended April 30, before pretax non-recurring charges of $9.2 million, according to H&R Block Inc, which owns 80.1 percent of CompuServe.
CompuServ had a loss in the third quarter of $14.2 million.

The one-time fourth quarter charges related primarily to a further consolidation of Columbus-area office facilities and the sale or write-down of certain equity investments in providers of content and technologies, H&R Block said.
CompuServe's earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, amortization and non-cash special charges improved to $12.6 million in the fourth quarter from $9.4 million in the third quarter.

"The improvement was driven by a four percentage-point increase in gross margin, from 36 percent in the third quarter to 40 percent in the most recent quarter," Frank Salizzoni, president of H&R Block, said in a statement.

For the full fiscal year, CompuServe reported a loss of $119.8 million, or $1.29 per share, on revenues of $842 million. The loss included $80.1 million of pretax charges relating to disposition of certain assets, the write-off of deferred subscriber acquisition costs, expenses for the write-off and withdrawal of WOW!, and the consolidation of facilities.
As majority owner, H&R Block's share of CompuServe's full-year loss was $96 million, or $0.91 per H&R Block share.
CompuServe's earnings for the prior fiscal year were $49.1 million, or $0.66 per share, on revenues of $793 million.
